explanation: She won Best Supporting Actress at the 1940 ceremony, held in a hotel where she was seated at a separate table from her co-stars. Butterfly McQueen played Prissy.

claims.text: Hattie McDaniel was the first Black performer to win an Academy Award, for her role as Mammy in Gone with the Wind (1939).
Butterfly McQueen, Ethel Waters and Dorothy Dandridge did not win an Oscar for Gone with the Wind.
Hattie McDaniel won the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress at the ceremony held in February 1940.
At the ceremony, at the Ambassador Hotel in Los Angeles, McDaniel was seated at a separate table from her Gone with the Wind co-stars.
Butterfly McQueen played Prissy in Gone with the Wind.
